newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ tax in 2050 could near 40 pct of GDP - report.
newsitem.headline: NZ tax in 2050 could near 40 pct of GDP - report.

text.p: New Zealand could face tax requirements of nearly 40 percent of gross domestic product by the middle of the next century as an ageing population puts pressure on health and retirement costs, a report released on Thursday said.

"At present gross expenditure on New Zealand Superannuation is about five percent of gross domestic product, which is manageable, but this percentage is expected to rise over the first half of the next century as a result of population ageing," said the 1997 retirement income report written by the Periodic Report Group, an independent body set up by the
"The cost of health services is also expected to expand," the report said. "These fiscal pressures could result in historically high tax revenue requirements, approaching 40 percent of GDP in 2050."

The report, released ahead of the September referendum on compulsory superannuation, found the current mix of a universal state funded scheme and tax-neutral voluntary savings was affordable with gradual adjustments.

It said that to deal with the prospect of rising costs, tax rates could be set higher to reduce debt, they could be increased as the higher spending pressures start to occur about 2015, or spending could be adjusted to reduce the pressures.
"We believe there is merit in considering all of these approaches."

It said it had modelled scenarios which would take the country through a gradual transition so the public provision of pensions and other government expenditure would be much less than 40 percent of GDP by 2050.
The report said it was important to re-establish a multi- party political accord on the shape of retirement whatever the outcome of the September referendum.
